title: Alo Meets Tara
subtitle: Reciprocal Pollination & First-Generation Prediction
question: How do we help two self-incompatible plants make viable seed across two pressurised chambers without cross-contaminating brushes or breaching pressure boundaries?
goal_one_line: Transfer pollen Tara->Alo with Brush A and Alo->Tara with Brush B across three dated runs, log seven daily care checks, and pre-register a stem-colour hypothesis.

first_time_explainer.title: Reciprocal Pollination Protocol
first_time_explainer.summary: Brassica rapa is self-incompatible: each flower needs pollen from a partner plant's anther placed on its own receptive stigma. Keep Brush A (Tara->Alo) and Brush B (Alo->Tara) in closed carriers, open one pressure door at a time (E1/A1 per complete cycle), and pre-register a stem-colour hypothesis before seeds mature.

learn.label: Learn · Protocol & Trade Study
learn.summary: Confirm flower anatomy (anther vs stigma), trade-study why chambers stay separate and brushes are labelled A and B, verify space weather GO, and rehearse single-boundary pressure order.

apply.label: Apply · Reciprocal Runs & 7-Day Care
apply.summary: Execute three dated reciprocal runs (30 Apr, 3 May, 6 May) at E1/A1 per cycle and log seven daily care observations without contaminating either stigma.

twist.label: Twist · Pre-Registered Stem Prediction
twist.summary: Record what stem colours may appear when purple-stemmed Alo and green-stemmed Tara cross, why genotypes are still unknown, and what future test will check the descendants.

structures.label: Anther (pollen sac)
structures.feedback: Pollen collected from the donor anther onto the clean brush tip.

structures.label: Stigma (receptive tip)
structures.feedback: Partner pollen transferred cleanly onto the recipient flower's receptive stigma.

structures.label: Yellow petal
structures.feedback: Touching a petal transfers no pollen. Collect from the donor anther and touch the partner plant's receptive stigma.

brushes.label: Brush A · Tara -> Alo
brushes.feedback: Brush A is dedicated to Tara -> Alo transfers inside Carrier A.

brushes.label: Brush B · Alo -> Tara
brushes.feedback: Brush B is dedicated to Alo -> Tara transfers inside Carrier B.

brushes.label: One unlabelled brush for both directions
brushes.feedback: With one brush you can't tell which pollen went where. Use Brush A for Tara->Alo and clean Brush B for Alo->Tara.

carrier_modes.label: Closed carrier · one pressure door at a time
carrier_modes.feedback: Closed carrier sealed; inner and outer boundaries open one at a time so pollen stays dry and rooms stay isolated.

carrier_modes.label: Carry open brush through corridor
carrier_modes.feedback: An unsealed brush loses pollen and risks contamination across rooms. Seal the carrier before moving.

carrier_modes.label: Put the two chambers together / open both doors
carrier_modes.feedback: Opening both boundaries or putting both plants in one chamber breaks isolation: a single leak or pathogen could wipe out both Alo and Tara.

weather_modes.label: Space weather GO verified (quiet solar window)
weather_modes.feedback: Space weather GO confirmed; corridor transfer between Bay 2 and the Greenhouse is safe.

weather_modes.label: Skip space-weather check
weather_modes.feedback: Verify space weather GO before opening the transfer route between Bay 2 and the Greenhouse.

p03_collect_tara_pollen.label: Collect Tara pollen from anther with Brush A

p03_seal_brush_a.label: Seal Brush A in closed carrier & pass one boundary at a time

p03_transfer_to_alo.label: Touch Alo's receptive stigma with Brush A

p03_collect_alo_pollen.label: Collect Alo pollen from anther with clean Brush B

p03_seal_brush_b.label: Seal Brush B in closed carrier & pass one boundary at a time

p03_transfer_to_tara.label: Touch Tara's receptive stigma with Brush B

p03_run_2_forward.label: Run 2 Forward · Tara anther -> Brush A -> Alo stigma (2046-05-03)

p03_run_2_reverse.label: Run 2 Reverse · Alo anther -> Brush B -> Tara stigma (2046-05-03)

p03_run_3_forward.label: Run 3 Forward · Tara anther -> Brush A -> Alo stigma (2046-05-06)

p03_run_3_reverse.label: Run 3 Reverse · Alo anther -> Brush B -> Tara stigma (2046-05-06)

care_dates.label: Day 5 · 04 May petal drop & swelling check

expectations.label: Both visible colours (purple and green stems) may appear
expectations.feedback: Valid expectation: with one purple-stemmed parent and one green-stemmed parent of unestablished genotype, both colours remain possible.

expectations.value: Every seedling will follow a guaranteed fixed ratio
expectations.label: Promise a guaranteed 100% purple or fixed 3:1 ratio now
expectations.feedback: We only know the two parents' visible stem colours, not whether either parent is homozygous or heterozygous. Do not promise a fixed ratio before observing the descendants.

expectations.value: Stems will turn yellow like the petals
expectations.label: Stems will turn bright yellow like flower petals
expectations.feedback: Petal yellow and stem purple/green are different traits. Record what you expect for purple vs green stems.

reasons.value: Alo has purple and Tara has green stems; the complete genotype is not established.
reasons.label: Alo has purple and Tara has green stems; the complete genotype is not established.
reasons.feedback: Accurate reasoning: visible phenotype alone does not establish the full underlying genotype of both founder plants.

reasons.value: Seeds only copy the mother plant's stem colour.
reasons.label: Each seed is a clone of whichever plant held the pod.
reasons.feedback: Reciprocal cross-pollination combines alleles from both donor pollen and recipient ovule—seedlings are not maternal clones.

future_tests.value: Compare descendant stem observations after seed harvest.
future_tests.label: Compare descendant stem observations after seed harvest (surprise: every plant one colour).
future_tests.feedback: Testable criterion registered: descendant stem counts after harvest will test the prediction.

future_tests.value: Decide now without counting future seedlings.
future_tests.label: Close the study today without counting future seedlings.
future_tests.feedback: A scientific prediction needs a future test: we must compare descendant stem observations after seed harvest.

feedback_messages.self_pollination: Cultivar self-incompatibility: Brassica rapa flowers reject their own pollen. Transfer pollen from the partner plant instead.
feedback_messages.wrong_brush_direction: Wrong brush for this direction: use Brush A only for Tara -> Alo and Brush B only for Alo -> Tara so pollen lineages stay distinct.
feedback_messages.dirty_brush: Brush tip is carrying unverified pollen; replace the tip with a clean sterile tip before collecting.
feedback_messages.unsealed_carrier: Seal the brush inside its closed carrier before crossing the pressure boundary.
feedback_messages.missing_weather_check: Confirm space weather is GO before starting a cross-chamber pollination transfer.
feedback_messages.petal_selected: Touching a petal transfers no pollen. Select the donor anther to collect pollen and the recipient stigma to deliver it.
feedback_messages.prediction_incomplete: Select your expectation, scientific reason, and future test in the Stem Prediction panel before locking in.

clues.label: Flower anatomy & self-incompatibility
clues.text: Anther holds pollen; stigma receives it. Brassica rapa is self-incompatible—each plant needs pollen from its partner.

clues.label: Single-boundary airlock & closed carrier
clues.text: Keep Alo and Tara in separate chambers so one fault cannot harm both. Seal the brush carrier and open one pressure door at a time (E1/A1 per cycle).

clues.label: Space-weather GO & 7-day care window
clues.text: Check space weather GO before each transfer on 30 Apr, 03 May, and 06 May, and log all 7 dated care visits.

clues.label: Brushes A/B & purple/green stems
clues.text: Use Brush A for Tara->Alo and Brush B for Alo->Tara. Alo has a purple stem and Tara has a green stem—write what we expect and what would surprise us.

pollination: A flower needs pollen from its partner.
Take pollen from the anther to the other plant’s stigma.
Use A for Tara→Alo and clean B for Alo→Tara.
prediction: What can two stem colours tell you, and what can't they?
Write what you expect and what would surprise you.
Example of the format: 'Both colours may appear. A surprise would be every plant one colour.'
